Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 44, verses 1–6:

Regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿Ha Mim (1) By the Clear Book (2) Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night; indeed, We were ever warning (3) In it is made distinct every wise matter (4) a command from Us. Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers] (5) as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (6)﴾

The explanation of His words ﴿Ha Mim, by the Clear Book﴾ has already been given, and His words ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾: He, exalted is His praise, swore by this Book that He sent it down during a blessed night.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about that night, which of the nights of the year it is. Some of them said: it is the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr).

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾: it is the Night of Power. The scrolls of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah was sent down six nights into Ramadan, the Psalms (al-Zabur) were sent down sixteen days into Ramadan, the Gospel (al-Injil) was sent down eighteen days into Ramadan, and the Furqan was sent down twenty-four days into Ramadan.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿in a blessed night﴾, he said: it is the Night of Power.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, mighty and majestic is He, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, indeed We were ever warning﴾: that night is the Night of Power, in which God sent down this Qur'an from the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab) in the Night of Power, and then sent it down upon the prophets [[In Fath al-Qadir by al-Shawkani (4: 554): "Qatadah said: the whole Qur'an was sent down in the Night of Power from the Mother of the Book, which is the Preserved Tablet, to the House of Honour in the lowest heaven, and then God sent it down upon His Prophet ﷺ over nights and days, across twenty-three years."]] over nights and days, and on other than the Night of Power.

Others said: rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban.

The correct view on this matter is the view of those who said that it means the Night of Power, because God, exalted is His mention, informed that this is so by His words ﴿indeed We were ever warning﴾: We warn by this Book which We sent down in the blessed night, of Our punishment befalling those among them who disbelieved, who did not turn back to Our monotheism and to singling Us out for divinity.

* *

As for His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾:

The people of interpretation differed concerning this night in which every wise matter is made distinct, similar to their difference concerning the blessed night, since the pronoun in His words ﴿In it﴾ refers to the blessed night. Some of them said: it is the Night of Power, in which the affair of the whole year is decreed: who will die, who will be born, who will be honoured, who will be humbled, and all the other affairs of the year.

Those who said this:

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum informed us, saying: I was with al-Hasan when a man said to him: "O Abu Sa'id, is the Night of Power in every Ramadan?" He said: "Yes, by God, it is indeed in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is made distinct; in it God decrees every term, provision and hope until its like [the following year]."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: a man said to al-Hasan while I was listening: "Tell me, is the Night of Power in every Ramadan?" He said: "Yes, by God, besides whom there is no god, it is indeed in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is made distinct; God decrees every term, creation and provision until its like."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Salim said, from 'Umar, the mawla of Ghafrah, who said: It is said that the one who is to die is recorded for the Angel of Death from the Night of Power to its like, because God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾ and He says ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾. He said: "You find a man marrying women and planting trees while his name is among the dead."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah, from Abu Malik, regarding His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: the affair of the year, from one year to the next, whether it is creation, provision, term, calamity, or the like.

[Ibn Bashshar] said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: It used to be said: "Await the decree in the month of Ramadan."

al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, regarding His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: He said: the affair of the year is arranged in the Night of Power.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: He said: On the Night of Power, every matter that will occur in the year, from one year to the next, is [decided]: life and death; provisions and calamities are all decreed in it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾, the Night of Power, ﴿in it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: "We used to be told that the affair of the year is made distinct in it, from one year to the next."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: It is the Night of Power, in which what will occur in the year is decreed, from one year to the next.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: I asked Mujahid: "Tell me about one of us who supplicates saying: 'O God, if my name is among the happy, then confirm it among them, and if it is among the wretched, then erase it from them and make it among the happy.'" He said: "Good." Then I met him after a year or more and asked him about this supplication, and he recited: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, indeed We were ever warning, in it is made distinct every wise matter﴾, and said: In the Night of Power is decreed what will occur in the year of provision or calamity; then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the book of happiness and wretchedness, it is fixed and does not change.

Others said: rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban.

Those who said this:

al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah and al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, both saying: al-Hasan ibn Isma'il al-Bajali narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from 'Ikrimah, regarding God's words, blessed and exalted is He, ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾, he said: On the night of the middle of Sha'ban, the affair of the year is determined in it; the living are separated from the dead, and the pilgrims are recorded, so that none is added to them and none is subtracted from them.

'Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhnas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Terms are cut off from Sha'ban to Sha'ban, so much so that a man marries and fathers children, while his name has already been listed among the dead."

Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to me, saying: Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "A man walks among the people while his name has been raised among the dead." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, indeed We were ever warning, in it is made distinct every wise matter﴾, and said: "In it is made distinct the affair of this world from one year to the next."

The more correct of the two views is the view of those who said that it is the Night of Power, due to what we have already explained, that the one meant by His words ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾ is the Night of Power, and the pronoun in His words ﴿in it﴾ refers to the blessed night.

By His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾ is meant: in this blessed night is decreed and separated every matter which God has decided for that year until its like in the following year. The word ḥakīm (wise) is placed in the sense of muḥkam (decided/firm), as He said: ﴿Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾, meaning: the decisive (muḥkam).

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it is accusative in the sense of "every matter is made distinct, a distinguishing and a command." He said: likewise His words ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾. He said: it is also permissible for raḥmah (mercy) to be accusative by the verb "sending" (mursilīn) acting upon it, making the mercy for the Prophet ﷺ.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, mighty and majestic is He, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, indeed We were ever warning﴾: that night is the Night of Power, in which God sent down this Qur'an from the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab) in the Night of Power, and then sent it down upon the prophets [[In Fath al-Qadir by al-Shawkani (4: 554): "Qatadah said: the whole Qur'an was sent down in the Night of Power from the Mother of the Book, which is the Preserved Tablet, to the House of Honour in the lowest heaven, and then God sent it down upon His Prophet ﷺ over nights and days, across twenty-three years."]] over nights and days, and on other than the Night of Power.

Others said: rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban.

The correct view on this matter is the view of those who said that it means the Night of Power, because God, exalted is His mention, informed that this is so by His words ﴿indeed We were ever warning﴾: We warn by this Book which We sent down in the blessed night, of Our punishment befalling those among them who disbelieved, who did not turn back to Our monotheism and to singling Us out for divinity.

* *

As for His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾:

The people of interpretation differed concerning this night in which every wise matter is made distinct, similar to their difference concerning the blessed night, since the pronoun in His words ﴿In it﴾ refers to the blessed night. Some of them said: it is the Night of Power, in which the affair of the whole year is decreed: who will die, who will be born, who will be honoured, who will be humbled, and all the other affairs of the year.

Those who said this:

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum informed us, saying: I was with al-Hasan when a man said to him: "O Abu Sa'id, is the Night of Power in every Ramadan?" He said: "Yes, by God, it is indeed in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is made distinct; in it God decrees every term, provision and hope until its like [the following year]."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: a man said to al-Hasan while I was listening: "Tell me, is the Night of Power in every Ramadan?" He said: "Yes, by God, besides whom there is no god, it is indeed in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is made distinct; God decrees every term, creation and provision until its like."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Salim said, from 'Umar, the mawla of Ghafrah, who said: It is said that the one who is to die is recorded for the Angel of Death from the Night of Power to its like, because God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾ and He says ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾. He said: "You find a man marrying women and planting trees while his name is among the dead."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah, from Abu Malik, regarding His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: the affair of the year, from one year to the next, whether it is creation, provision, term, calamity, or the like.

[Ibn Bashshar] said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: It used to be said: "Await the decree in the month of Ramadan."

al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, regarding His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: He said: the affair of the year is arranged in the Night of Power.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: He said: On the Night of Power, every matter that will occur in the year, from one year to the next, is [decided]: life and death; provisions and calamities are all decreed in it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾, the Night of Power, ﴿in it is made distinct every wise matter﴾: "We used to be told that the affair of the year is made distinct in it, from one year to the next."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: It is the Night of Power, in which what will occur in the year is decreed, from one year to the next.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: I asked Mujahid: "Tell me about one of us who supplicates saying: 'O God, if my name is among the happy, then confirm it among them, and if it is among the wretched, then erase it from them and make it among the happy.'" He said: "Good." Then I met him after a year or more and asked him about this supplication, and he recited: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, indeed We were ever warning, in it is made distinct every wise matter﴾, and said: In the Night of Power is decreed what will occur in the year of provision or calamity; then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the book of happiness and wretchedness, it is fixed and does not change.

Others said: rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban.

Those who said this:

al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah and al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, both saying: al-Hasan ibn Isma'il al-Bajali narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from 'Ikrimah, regarding God's words, blessed and exalted is He, ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾, he said: On the night of the middle of Sha'ban, the affair of the year is determined in it; the living are separated from the dead, and the pilgrims are recorded, so that none is added to them and none is subtracted from them.

'Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhnas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Terms are cut off from Sha'ban to Sha'ban, so much so that a man marries and fathers children, while his name has already been listed among the dead."

Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to me, saying: Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "A man walks among the people while his name has been raised among the dead." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, indeed We were ever warning, in it is made distinct every wise matter﴾, and said: "In it is made distinct the affair of this world from one year to the next."

The more correct of the two views is the view of those who said that it is the Night of Power, due to what we have already explained, that the one meant by His words ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾ is the Night of Power, and the pronoun in His words ﴿in it﴾ refers to the blessed night.

By His words ﴿In it is made distinct every wise matter﴾ is meant: in this blessed night is decreed and separated every matter which God has decided for that year until its like in the following year. The word ḥakīm (wise) is placed in the sense of muḥkam (decided/firm), as He said: ﴿Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾, meaning: the decisive (muḥkam).

* *

As for His words ﴿a command from Us. Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers]﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: in this blessed night every wise matter is made distinct, a command from Us.

The grammarians differed about the reason for the accusative case of the word ﴿amran﴾. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: it is accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of "We sent it down": "amran wa-raḥmatan." Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it is accusative in the sense of "every matter is made distinct, a distinguishing and a command." He said: likewise His words ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾. He said: it is also permissible for raḥmah (mercy) to be accusative by the verb "sending" (mursilīn) acting upon it, making the mercy for the Prophet ﷺ.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers]﴾

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Indeed We were ever sending Our Messenger Muhammad ﷺ to Our servants as a mercy from your Lord, O Muhammad. ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He says: Indeed God, blessed and exalted, is the All-Hearing of what these polytheists say concerning what We sent down of Our Book and what We sent of Our messengers to them, and of other than that of their speech and the speech of others; the All-Knowing of what their hearts conceal, and of other than that of their affairs and the affairs of others.

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain﴾ (7) ﴿There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾ (8) ﴿But they are in doubt, playing﴾ (9).

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾. The reciters of Medina and most of the reciters of Basra recited "Rabbu as-samawati" with a nominative (raf') ending, following the i'rab of "al-Rabb" to the i'rab of "al-Samee' al-'Aleem" (the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing). The reciters of Kufa and some of the Meccans in general recited "Rabba as-samawati" with a genitive (khafd) ending, as a repetition (radd) of "al-Rabb" in His, may His majesty be exalted, words ﴿a mercy from your Lord﴾.

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known recitations, sound in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

By His words ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: the One who sent down this Book, O Muhammad, upon you, and sent you to these polytheists, is a mercy from your Lord, the Owner of the seven heavens, the earth, and everything that is between them.

* *

As for His words ﴿if you are certain﴾

He says: if you are certain of the truth of what I have told you, that your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and that the One whose attributes these are is God, and that this Qur'an is His revelation, and that Muhammad (ﷺ) is His messenger, then it is true certainty. So be certain of it as you are certain of the realities of things other than it.

* *

As for His words ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾

He says: there is no worshipped one for you, O people, other than the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so do not worship anything besides Him, for worship is fit for none other than Him and is not befitting for anything else. ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾ means: He is the One who gives life to whatever He wills and causes death to whatever He wills of what was alive.

* *

As for His words ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones﴾

He says: He is the Owner of you and the Owner of those who passed before you, your forefathers of old. He says: so this One, whose attributes these are, is the Lord; worship Him alone, not your gods that have no power to harm or benefit.

* *

As for His words ﴿But they are in doubt, playing﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: they are not certain of the truth of what is said to them and what they are told of these reports, meaning the polytheists of Quraysh. Rather, they are in doubt about it, so they amuse themselves with their doubt concerning what they are told.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 44, verses 10–12:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke (10) enveloping the people; this is a painful punishment (11) Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers (12)﴾

By His saying, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿So watch﴾, He means: wait, O Muhammad, for these polytheists of your people who are in doubt, playing. It is from ifti'āl (the reflexive verb form), from "raqabtuhu," meaning: when I waited for him and guarded him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ḥadathanā Bishr, who said: Thanā Yazīd, who said: Thanā Sa'īd, from Qatādah, regarding ﴿So watch﴾: that is, wait.

* *

And His saying ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning what it is that God, mighty and majestic, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to watch for, and informed him that the sky would bring forth visible smoke on it: that is, what day is it, and when is it? And concerning the meaning of the smoke mentioned in this passage. Some of them said: it was when the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed to his Lord, blessed and exalted, against Quraysh, that He would seize them with years like the years of Joseph, and they were seized by famine. They said: by the smoke was meant what afflicted them then in their sight from the severity of hunger, a darkness like the appearance of smoke.

Mention of those who said that:

Ḥaddathanī ʿĪsā ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā al-Ramlī, who said: Thanā Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said: We entered the mosque, and there was a man telling stories to his companions, saying: ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾. Do you know what that smoke is? That is a smoke that comes on the Day of Resurrection, which seizes the hearing and sight of the hypocrites, and the believers will be affected by it like a cold. He said: We came to Ibn Masʿūd and mentioned that to him, and he was lying down; he was startled, sat up, and said: God, mighty and majestic, said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend﴾. Indeed, it is part of knowledge that a man says of what he does not know: "God knows best." I will tell you about that. When Quraysh were slow to accept Islam and defied the Messenger of God ﷺ, he prayed against them for years like the years of Joseph, and they were afflicted by hardship and hunger until they ate bones and carrion, and they would raise their eyes to the sky and see nothing but smoke.

God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, enveloping the people; this is a painful punishment﴾. Then they said: ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers﴾. God, His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed, you will return. The day We seize with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution﴾. He said: They returned on the day of Badr, and God took retribution from them.

Ḥaddathanī ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī, who said: Thanā Mālik ibn Suʿayr, who said: Thanā al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said: There was a man in the mosque reminding people, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of ʿĪsā from Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā, except that he said: "He took retribution on the day of Badr, and that is the greatest seizure."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Ḥumayd and ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, who both said: Thanā Jarīr, from Manṣūr, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Masrūq, who said: We were sitting with ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, and he was lying down among us. A man came to him and said: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a storyteller at the gates of Kinda is telling stories and claims that the sign of the smoke will come and seize the breaths of the disbelievers, and the believers will be affected by it like a cold." ʿAbdullāh rose, sat up, and he was angry, and said: "O people, fear God. Whoever knows something, let him say what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say: God knows best."

ʿAmr said: It is better for one of you to say, regarding what he does not know, "God knows best," and there is nothing wrong with one of you saying, regarding what he does not know, "I do not know," for God, mighty and majestic, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend﴾. When the Prophet ﷺ saw the people turning away, he said: "O God, seven years like the seven of Joseph." So a drought struck them that destroyed everything, until they ate hides, carrion, and corpses, and one of them would look at the sky and see smoke from hunger. Then Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you came commanding obedience and maintaining ties of kinship, and your people have perished, so pray to God for them." God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾ … until His saying ﴿you will return﴾. He said: Then it was removed from them. ﴿The day We seize with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution﴾: the seizure is the day of Badr, and the smoke of the verse of Rome and the verse of the smoke have passed, and the seizure and the penalty (al-lizām).

Ḥaddathanī Abū al-Sāʾib, who said: Thanā Abū Muʿāwiyah, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbdullāh said: Five have passed: the smoke, the penalty (al-lizām), the seizure, the moon, and the Romans.

Ḥaddathanā Abū Kurayb, who said: Thanā Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿĀṣim, who said: I attended a funeral in which Zayd ibn ʿAlī was present, and he began to narrate that day, and said: "Indeed, the smoke will come before the Day of Resurrection, and it will seize the nose of the believer with a cold, and seize the ears of the disbeliever." I said: "May God have mercy on you, our companion ʿAbdullāh has said other than this." He said: "The smoke has already passed," and he recited this verse: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, enveloping the people; this is a painful punishment﴾. He said: The people were struck by hardship until a man would see smoke between himself and the sky, and that is His saying ﴿So watch﴾. And thus ʿAbdullāh recited up to His saying ﴿believers﴾. He said: ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little﴾. I said to Zayd: "They returned," and God returned them to Badr, and that is His saying ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾. So that is the day of Badr. He said: "By God, he accepted it." ʿĀṣim said: A man replied to him, and Zayd said, may God have mercy on him: "Indeed the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'There will come to you narrators; whatever agrees with the Qur'an, take it, and whatever is other than that, leave it.'"

Ḥaddathanā Ibn al-Muthannā, who said: Thanā Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said: Thanā Dāwūd, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: "The seizure of the greatest is the day of Badr, and the smoke has passed."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Bashshār, who said: Thanā Ibn Abī ʿAdī, from ʿAwf, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliyah say: "Indeed the smoke has passed."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Thanā Salamah, from ʿAmr, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "The smoke passed, for years that struck them."

Ḥaddathanī Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Thanā Ibn ʿUlayyah, who said: Thanā Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, who said: I was informed that Ibn Masʿūd used to say: "The smoke has passed; it was years like the years of Joseph."

Ḥaddathanī Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, who said: Thanā Abū ʿĀṣim, who said: Thanā ʿĪsā; and Ḥaddathanī al-Ḥārith, who said: Thanā al-Ḥasan, who said: Thanā Warqāʾ, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾: he said: the drought and the withholding of rain from the disbelievers of Quraysh, up to His saying ﴿indeed, we are believers﴾.

Ḥaddathanā Bishr, who said: Thanā Yazīd, who said: Thanā Saʿīd, from Qatādah: ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾: he said: Ibn Masʿūd used to say: "The smoke has passed, and it was years like the years of Joseph," ﴿enveloping the people; this is a painful punishment﴾.

I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾: "The matter of the smoke has passed."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Thanā Jarīr, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbdullāh ﴿the day We seize with the greatest seizure﴾: he said: "The day of Badr."

And others said: The smoke is one of the signs of God, sent upon His servants before the coming of the Hour; it enters the hearing of those who disbelieve in it, and it affects those who believe in it like a cold. They said: It has not yet come, and it is coming.

Mention of those who said that:

The day We seize with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution﴾. He said: They returned on the day of Badr, and God took retribution from them.

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Ḥumayd and ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, who both said: Thanā Jarīr, from Manṣūr, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Masrūq, who said: We were sitting with ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, and he was lying down among us. A man came to him and said: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a storyteller at the gates of Kinda is telling stories and claims that the sign of the smoke will come and seize the breaths of the disbelievers, and the believers will be affected by it like a cold." ʿAbdullāh rose, sat up, and he was angry, and said: "O people, fear God. Whoever knows something, let him say what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say: God knows best."

ʿAmr said: It is better for one of you to say, regarding what he does not know, "God knows best," and there is nothing wrong with one of you saying, regarding what he does not know, "I do not know," for God, mighty and majestic, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend﴾. When the Prophet ﷺ saw the people turning away, he said: "O God, seven years like the seven of Joseph." So a drought struck them that destroyed everything, until they ate hides, carrion, and corpses, and one of them would look at the sky and see smoke from hunger. Then Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you came commanding obedience and maintaining ties of kinship, and your people have perished, so pray to God for them." God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾ … until His saying ﴿you will return﴾. He said: Then it was removed from them. ﴿The day We seize with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution﴾: the seizure is the day of Badr, and the smoke of the verse of Rome and the verse of the smoke have passed, and the seizure and the penalty (al-lizām).

Ḥaddathanī Abū al-Sāʾib, who said: Thanā Abū Muʿāwiyah, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, who said: ʿAbdullāh said: Five have passed: the smoke, the penalty (al-lizām), the seizure, the moon, and the Romans.

Ḥaddathanā Abū Kurayb, who said: Thanā Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿĀṣim, who said: I attended a funeral in which Zayd ibn ʿAlī was present, and he began to narrate that day, and said: "Indeed, the smoke will come before the Day of Resurrection, and it will seize the nose of the believer with a cold, and seize the ears of the disbeliever." I said: "May God have mercy on you, our companion ʿAbdullāh has said other than this." He said: "The smoke has already passed," and he recited this verse: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, enveloping the people; this is a painful punishment﴾. He said: The people were struck by hardship until a man would see smoke between himself and the sky, and that is His saying ﴿So watch﴾. And thus ʿAbdullāh recited up to His saying ﴿believers﴾. He said: ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little﴾. I said to Zayd: "They returned," and God returned them to Badr, and that is His saying ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾. So that is the day of Badr. He said: "By God, he accepted it." ʿĀṣim said: A man replied to him, and Zayd said, may God have mercy on him: "Indeed the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'There will come to you narrators; whatever agrees with the Qur'an, take it, and whatever is other than that, leave it.'"

Ḥaddathanā Ibn al-Muthannā, who said: Thanā Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said: Thanā Dāwūd, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: "The seizure of the greatest is the day of Badr, and the smoke has passed."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Bashshār, who said: Thanā Ibn Abī ʿAdī, from ʿAwf, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliyah say: "Indeed the smoke has passed."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Thanā Salamah, from ʿAmr, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "The smoke passed, for years that struck them."

Ḥaddathanī Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Thanā Ibn ʿUlayyah, who said: Thanā Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, who said: I was informed that Ibn Masʿūd used to say: "The smoke has passed; it was years like the years of Joseph."

Ḥaddathanī Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, who said: Thanā Abū ʿĀṣim, who said: Thanā ʿĪsā; and Ḥaddathanī al-Ḥārith, who said: Thanā al-Ḥasan, who said: Thanā Warqāʾ, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾: he said: the drought and the withholding of rain from the disbelievers of Quraysh, up to His saying ﴿indeed, we are believers﴾.

Ḥaddathanā Bishr, who said: Thanā Yazīd, who said: Thanā Saʿīd, from Qatādah: ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾: he said: Ibn Masʿūd used to say: "The smoke has passed, and it was years like the years of Joseph," ﴿enveloping the people; this is a painful punishment﴾.

I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾: "The matter of the smoke has passed."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Thanā Jarīr, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbdullāh ﴿the day We seize with the greatest seizure﴾: he said: "The day of Badr."

And others said: The smoke is one of the signs of God, sent upon His servants before the coming of the Hour; it enters the hearing of those who disbelieve in it, and it affects those who believe in it like a cold. They said: It has not yet come, and it is coming.

Mention of those who said that:

Ḥaddathanī Wāṣil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said: Thanā Ibn Fuḍayl, from al-Walīd ibn Jumayʿ, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Baylamān, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The smoke will come out, and it will seize the believer like a cold, and it will enter the ears of the disbeliever and the hypocrite, until he becomes like a roasted head.

Ḥaddathanī Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Thanā Ibn ʿUlayyah, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, who said: I went one day to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: "I did not sleep last night until morning." I said: "Why?" He said: "They said: the star with the tail has risen, and I feared the smoke had come upon us at night, so I did not sleep until morning."

Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Bazīʿ, who said: Thanā Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal, from ʿAwf, who said: al-Ḥasan said: "Indeed the smoke remains among the signs; when the smoke comes, it will make the disbeliever swell until it comes out of every ear, and it will seize the believer like a cold."

Ḥaddathanā Ibn Bashshār, who said: Thanā ʿUthmān, that is Ibn al-Haytham, who said: Thanā ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan, similarly.

Ḥaddathanā Bishr, who said: Thanā Yazīd, who said: Thanā Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from Abū Saʿīd, who said: "The smoke will stir up the people. As for the believer, it will seize him like a cold. As for the disbeliever, it will agitate him until it comes out of every opening of his." He said: Some people of knowledge used to say: "Then the likeness of the earth on that day will be only like a house in which a fire is kindled, with no gap in it."

Ḥaddathanī ʿIṣām ibn Rawwād ibn al-Jarrāḥ, who said: Thanī my father, who said: Thanā Sufyān ibn Saʿīd al-Thawrī, who said: Thanā Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from Rib'ī ibn Ḥarrāsh, who said: I heard Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The first of the signs is the Dajjal, and the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and a fire that comes out from the bottom of ʿAdn Abyan, driving the people to the place of gathering, napping with them when they nap, and the smoke." Ḥudhayfah said: "O Messenger of God, what is the smoke?" The Messenger of God ﷺ recited the verse: ﴿the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, enveloping the people; this is a painful punishment﴾. It will fill what is between the east and the west, and remain forty days and nights. As for the believer, it will affect him like a cold. As for the disbeliever, he will be like a drunkard, coming out of his nostrils, ears, and rear."

Ḥaddathanī Muḥammad ibn ʿAwf, who said: Thanā Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, who said: Thanī my father, who said: Thanī Ḍamḍam ibn Zurʿah, from Sharīḥ ibn ʿUbayd, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed your Lord has warned you of three: the smoke, which seizes the believer like a cold and seizes the disbeliever so that he swells until it comes out of every opening of his; the second is the beast; and the third is the Dajjal."

The more correct of the two sayings concerning this is what was narrated from Ibn Masʿūd, that the smoke which God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to watch for is what afflicted his people with hardship when he prayed against them, according to what Ibn Masʿūd described of it, unless the report of Ḥudhayfah which we mentioned from him from the Messenger of God ﷺ is sound. And if it is sound, then the Messenger of God ﷺ knows best what God revealed to him, and no one's saying is valid alongside what is authentically transmitted from him.

I have not testified to its soundness only because Muḥammad ibn Khalaf al-ʿAsqalānī informed me that he asked Rawwād about this hadith, whether he heard it from Sufyān. He said: No. I said: Did you read it to him? He said: No. I said: Was it read to him while you were present and he acknowledged it? He said: No. I said: Then from where did you get it? He said: A group of people brought it to me, presented it to me, and said: "Listen to it from us," and they read it to me, then they left and related it from me, or as he said. Therefore, when I mentioned this, I did not testify to its soundness. Rather, I said: the saying that ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said is more correct as an interpretation of the verse, because God, mighty and majestic, threatened the polytheists of Quraysh with the smoke, and His saying to His Prophet ﷺ ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾ is within the context of God's address to the disbelievers of Quraysh and His rebuke of them for their polytheism, saying: ﴿There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death; your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones. But they are in doubt, playing﴾. Then He followed that with His saying to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾, a command from Him to him to be patient until His punishment comes to them, and a threat to the polytheists. So it is more fitting that it be what He had already brought upon them, since it was a threat to them, than that He postponed it for others.

Moreover, it is not impossible that He brought upon the disbelievers what He threatened them with, and that He will bring about another smoke later, as the reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ are, in our view, likewise indicating, for the reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ have been mutually reinforcing that it will happen. Indeed what ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd related from him has already occurred, so both reports narrated from the Messenger of God ﷺ are sound.

If the interpretation of the verse in this place is what we have said, and since what we have said is the preferable of the two interpretations, then its meaning is clear: So watch, O Muhammad, for the polytheists of your people, the day the sky brings them trial that will befall them for their disbelief, like a smoke clearly recognizable as smoke to anyone who observes it. ﴿Enveloping the people﴾: that is, it covers their sight with the hardship that afflicts them. ﴿This is a painful punishment﴾: meaning that they say, because of the distress and hardship that has reached them: "This is a painful punishment." Painful means causing pain. The verb "they say" is omitted from the speech, being understood by the listeners from the context.

* *

And His saying ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment﴾

This means that the disbelievers who are struck by that hardship humble themselves before their Lord, asking Him to remove that hardship from them, and they say: "If You remove it, we will believe in You and worship You alone, rather than every other object of worship," as He, exalted is His praise, reported about them: ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 44, verses 13–15:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿How will they have the reminder, when there has already come to them a clear Messenger? (13) Then they turned away from him and said, "A taught one, a madman!" (14) Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little, but you will return (to disbelief). (15)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: By what means will these polytheists have remembrance after the descent of the affliction upon them, when they had turned away from Our Messenger when he came to them, turning their backs on him, not taking heed of what is recited to them from Our Book, nor being admonished by what he admonishes them with from Our proofs, and saying: "He is only a madman who has been taught (this) speech" [[In the original: "على" in place of "علم" (taught). This is a scribal error.]].

And in accordance with what we have said regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿How will they have the reminder?﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿How will they have the reminder?﴾: he said: "How for them?"

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿How will they have the reminder?﴾: "After this affliction has befallen them."

And in accordance with what we have said also regarding His saying ﴿Then they turned away from him and said, "A taught one, a madman!"﴾, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Then they turned away from him and said, "A taught one, a madman!"﴾, he said: "They turned away from Muhammad, peace be upon him, and said: 'A taught one, a madman.'"

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little, but you will return (to disbelief)﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to these polytheists, of whom He reported that they seek His help against the smoke that descends and the punishment that has befallen them through hardship, and whom He reported as making a covenant with Him that "if the punishment is removed from them, they will believe": "Indeed, We will remove the punishment": meaning the harm that has descended upon them, by the fertility We will bring them. "A little, but you will return": He says: "Indeed you, O polytheists, when I remove from you the harm you have, you will not fulfil what you promise and what you covenant with your Lord of faith. Rather, you will return to your misguidance and your deviation, as you were before the removal of what afflicted you."

And Qatadah used to say: its meaning is: "Indeed you will return to the punishment of Allah."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related this to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from him (Qatadah).

As for those who said that the reference in His saying ﴿On the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾ is to the smoke itself, they said in this place that what is meant by "the punishment" in His saying ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment﴾ is: the smoke.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little﴾: "meaning the smoke."

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little﴾: "He has done so; the smoke was removed when it was."

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, you will return﴾:

He said: "It was removed from them, and they returned."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, you will return﴾: "to the punishment of Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 44, verse 16–18:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿On the Day We will strike the greatest striking; indeed, We will take retribution﴾ (16). ﴿And We had already tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger﴾ (17). ﴿[Saying], "Deliver to me the servants of Allah. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger"﴾ (18).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed you, O polytheists, if We remove from you the punishment that has descended upon you and the harm that has befallen you, and you then return to your disbelief and break the covenant you made with your Lord, We will take retribution from you on the Day We strike you with Our greatest striking in the hastened life of this world, and destroy you. Allah removed the punishment from them, and they returned, so His, the Majestic and Praised One's, greatest striking struck them in this world, and He destroyed them by killing them with the sword.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning "the greatest striking." Some of them said: It is Allah's striking of the polytheists of Quraysh on the Day of Badr.

Mention of those who said that:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "These are a criminal people."﴾ [22] ﴿"So travel by night with My servants; indeed you will be pursued."﴾ [23] ﴿"And leave the sea parted; indeed they are an army to be drowned."﴾ [24]

His saying, may He be remembered, means: Moses called upon his Lord when they denied him, did not believe in him, did not let the servants of God go to him, and intended to kill him, saying that these people, meaning Pharaoh and his folk, ﴿are a criminal people﴾, meaning: they are polytheists who disbelieve in God.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So travel by night with My servants﴾:

In the speech there is an omitted element, which is dispensed with by the indication of what has been mentioned, and it is: his Lord answered him by saying to him, "Travel, since the matter is so, with My servants," and they are the Children of Israel. The meaning of the speech is: travel with My servants who affirmed you, believed in you, and followed you, apart from those among them who denied you and refused to accept what you brought them of advice from you. The people who were of this description on that day were the Children of Israel. And He said, ﴿by night﴾, because the meaning of that is: travel with them by night before morning.

* *

As for His saying ﴿indeed you will be pursued﴾:

He says: Indeed Pharaoh and his folk, the Copts, will pursue you when you depart from their city and their land, following your traces.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾:

He says: When you and your companions have crossed the sea, leave it still in the state in which it was when you entered it. It has been said that God, may He be remembered, said this to Moses after he had brought the Children of Israel across the sea. So, since that is the case, there is an omitted element in the speech, which is: Moses journeyed by night with My servants and brought them across the sea, and then after he had crossed it, We said to him, and he intended to return the sea to the condition it was in before it split: leave it parted.

Mention of those who said that God, the Mighty and Majestic, said this to Moses ﷺ after he had crossed the sea with his people:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "These are a criminal people"﴾ until ﴿indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾, he said: When the last of the Children of Israel came out, the Prophet of God ﷺ wanted to strike the sea with his staff so that it would return as it was, fearing that the people of Pharaoh would catch up with them. So it was said to him, ﴿And leave the sea parted; indeed they are an army to be drowned.﴾

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: When he had crossed the sea, he turned back to strike the sea with his staff so that it would close up, and he feared that Pharaoh and his armies would follow him. So it was said to him: ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾ as it is, ﴿indeed they are an army to be drowned.﴾

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of ar-Rahw. Some of them said: its meaning is: leave it in its form and condition in which it was.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾ he said: it means "as a path" (samtan).

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted; indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾ he said: Ar-rahw: that it be left as it was, for they will not escape from behind it.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Humayd informed us, from Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from his father, that Ibn Abbas asked Ka'b about the saying of God ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, and he said: "a way."

Others said: rather, its meaning is: leave it easy.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: easy.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: It is said: ar-rahw: the easy.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Huramiyy ibn Umarah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Umarah informed me, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, concerning the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: smooth (damathan).

* I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say, Ubayd, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: easy and smooth.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: it is the easy.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: leave it dry and firm.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Shu'bah, from Simak, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: firm (jaddan).

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Simak, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: dry as it was after he struck it; he means: do not command it to return; leave it until the last of them has entered.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿rahwan﴾, he said: a dry way.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, as it is, a dry way.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 44, verse 22–24:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "These are a criminal people."﴾ [22] ﴿"So travel by night with My servants; indeed you will be pursued."﴾ [23] ﴿"And leave the sea parted; indeed they are an army to be drowned."﴾ [24]

His saying, may He be remembered, means: Moses called upon his Lord when they denied him, did not believe in him, did not let the servants of God go to him, and intended to kill him, saying that these people, meaning Pharaoh and his folk, ﴿are a criminal people﴾, meaning: they are polytheists who disbelieve in God.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So travel by night with My servants﴾:

In the speech there is an omitted element, which is dispensed with by the indication of what has been mentioned, and it is: his Lord answered him by saying to him, "Travel, since the matter is so, with My servants," and they are the Children of Israel. The meaning of the speech is: travel with My servants who affirmed you, believed in you, and followed you, apart from those among them who denied you and refused to accept what you brought them of advice from you. The people who were of this description on that day were the Children of Israel. And He said, ﴿by night﴾, because the meaning of that is: travel with them by night before morning.

* *

As for His saying ﴿indeed you will be pursued﴾:

He says: Indeed Pharaoh and his folk, the Copts, will pursue you when you depart from their city and their land, following your traces.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾:

He says: When you and your companions have crossed the sea, leave it still in the state in which it was when you entered it. It has been said that God, may He be remembered, said this to Moses after he had brought the Children of Israel across the sea. So, since that is the case, there is an omitted element in the speech, which is: Moses journeyed by night with My servants and brought them across the sea, and then after he had crossed it, We said to him, and he intended to return the sea to the condition it was in before it split: leave it parted.

Mention of those who said that God, the Mighty and Majestic, said this to Moses ﷺ after he had crossed the sea with his people:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "These are a criminal people"﴾ until ﴿indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾, he said: When the last of the Children of Israel came out, the Prophet of God ﷺ wanted to strike the sea with his staff so that it would return as it was, fearing that the people of Pharaoh would catch up with them. So it was said to him, ﴿And leave the sea parted; indeed they are an army to be drowned.﴾

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: When he had crossed the sea, he turned back to strike the sea with his staff so that it would close up, and he feared that Pharaoh and his armies would follow him. So it was said to him: ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾ as it is, ﴿indeed they are an army to be drowned.﴾

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of ar-Rahw. Some of them said: its meaning is: leave it in its form and condition in which it was.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾ he said: it means "as a path" (samtan).

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted; indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾ he said: Ar-rahw: that it be left as it was, for they will not escape from behind it.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Humayd informed us, from Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from his father, that Ibn Abbas asked Ka'b about the saying of God ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, and he said: "a way."

Others said: rather, its meaning is: leave it easy.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: easy.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: It is said: ar-rahw: the easy.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Huramiyy ibn Umarah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Umarah informed me, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, concerning the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: smooth (damathan).

* I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say, Ubayd, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: easy and smooth.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: it is the easy.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: leave it dry and firm.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Shu'bah, from Simak, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: firm (jaddan).

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Simak, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, he said: dry as it was after he struck it; he means: do not command it to return; leave it until the last of them has entered.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿rahwan﴾, he said: a dry way.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And leave the sea parted﴾, as it is, a dry way.

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the saying of those who said its meaning is: leave it in its form as it is, in the state in which it was when you traversed it. This is because ar-rahw in the speech of the Arabs means stillness, as the poet said:

It is as if the people of Hujr are looking, when will they see me going out,
A bird that saw a hawk, its blood-splattered, and its mother went out, parted, to a feast.

Meaning: in stillness. And if that is its meaning, then undoubtedly it is left easy and smooth, and a dry path, because the Children of Israel crossed it when they crossed it, and so it is. So if the sea is left parted, still as it was when Moses crossed it, unstirred, then undoubtedly it is in the description that has been mentioned.

* *

As for His saying ﴿indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾:

He says: Indeed Pharaoh and his folk are an army, which God will drown in the sea.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind (25), and crops and a noble station (26), and luxury in which they had been delighting (27). Thus We caused other people to inherit them (28).﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: How much Pharaoh and his people of the Copts left behind after their destruction and Allah's drowning of them, of gardens and trees, which are the gardens (jannat), and springs, meaning: the sources of what gushed forth in their gardens, and crops standing in their fields, ﴿and a noble station﴾, meaning: and a place they used to occupy that was honorable and noble.

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of God's describing that station as noble. Some of them said: He described it thus for its honor, for it was the station of kings and rulers, and they said: what is meant by it is the pulpits (al-manabir).

Mention of those who said that:

Jafar ibn Ibnat Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir narrated to us, from his father, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and a noble station﴾, he said: the pulpits.

Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿and a noble station﴾, he said: the pulpits.

Others said: He described that station as noble for its beauty and splendor.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and a noble station﴾: that is, beautiful.

* *

And His words ﴿and luxury in which they had been delighting﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: and they were removed from a luxury in which they had been delighting, enjoying themselves and living in ease.

The reciters differed in the reading of His words ﴿fakihin﴾. The majority of the reciters of the principal cities read it ﴿fakihin﴾ (with alif), according to the meaning I have described. Abu Ja'far al-Qari (Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa') read ﴿fakihin﴾ [as one word differs], and Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, al-Hasan and Abu Ja'far al-Madani read ﴿fakihin﴾ [without alif], with the meaning: exultant and insolent.

The correct reading in my view is the reading upon which the reciters of the principal cities agree, which is ﴿fakihin﴾ with alif, meaning: living in ease.

The people of interpretation also said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and luxury in which they had been delighting﴾: living in ease. He said: Yes, by Allah, Allah removed them from their gardens, springs and crops until He cast them into the sea.

* *

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 44, verses 29–31:

The interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they reprieved﴾ (29).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: the heaven and the earth did not weep over these people whom Allah drowned in the sea, namely Pharaoh and his people. It is also said that the weeping of the heaven is the reddening of its horizons.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, from al-Suddi, who said: When al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) was killed, the heaven wept over him, and its weeping was its reddening.

* 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', regarding His saying, ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾, he said: Its weeping is the reddening of its horizons.

It is also said: ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾ was said because when a believer dies, the heaven and the earth weep for him for forty mornings. They did not weep for Pharaoh and his people, because they had no righteous deed that would ascend to Allah, so the heaven would weep for them, and there was no place of worship on the earth, so the earth would weep for them.

The people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: O Abu 'Abbas, what do you think of the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they reprieved﴾? Do the heaven and the earth weep over anyone? He said: Yes. Indeed, there is no creature except that it has a gate in the heaven from which its provision descends and through which its deed ascends. When the believer dies, the gate of heaven through which his deed used to ascend and his provision used to descend is closed, and it weeps over him; and when the place of his prayer on the earth, where he used to pray and remember Allah, misses him, it weeps over him. As for the people of Pharaoh, there were no good traces of them on the earth, and no good used to ascend to the heaven from them. He said: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman and Yahya narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: It used to be said: The earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

* Yahya ibn Talhah narrated to me, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: I was told that when the believer dies, the earth weeps over him for forty mornings.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Bukayr ibn Abi al-Sumayt narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he used to say: The spots of the earth from which his deed used to ascend to the heaven weep over him after his death, meaning the believer.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾, he said: Indeed, there is no one except that he has a gate in the heaven where his provision descends and his deed ascends. When he is missed, the places where he used to prostrate on the earth weep over him. As for the people of Pharaoh, they had no righteous deed on the earth that would be accepted from them and ascend to Allah, mighty and majestic. Mujahid said: The earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: It used to be said: When the believer dies, the earth weeps over him for forty mornings.

* Yahya ibn Talhah narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd al-Hadrami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange. Unquestionably, there is no strangeness for the believer. No believer dies in a state of estrangement, in which his weepers are absent from him, except that the heaven and the earth weep over him." Allah had indeed tested them with both meanings together, and it is permissible that He meant by it their being tested with both. Given that the matter is as we have described, the correct statement concerning it is that we say as the One whose praise is great said: that He tested them.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And We gave them of the signs that which contained a clear trial﴾, and he recited ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial; and to Us you will be returned﴾, and said: "a clear trial for those who believed in them and those who disbelieved in them, a test with which We try them, We examine them with a test of trial, We test them with good and evil, We test them to see who among them believes in the signs that came to them, benefits from them, and who squanders them."

The most correct of these statements, in our view, is to say: Allah informed that He gave the Children of Israel of the signs that which contained their being tried and tested. Trial and testing may come through ease and may come through hardship, and we have no proof from report or reason that He meant one of these to the exclusion of the other. Allah had indeed tested them with both meanings together, and it is permissible that He meant by it their being tested with both. Given that the matter is as we have described, the correct statement concerning it is that we say as the One whose praise is great said: that He tested them.

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ ﴿We did not create them except with truth, but most of them do not know.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth﴾, the seven [heavens] and the earths, and what is between them of creation, in play.

* *

As for His words ﴿We did not create them except with truth﴾:

He says: We did not create the heavens and the earth except with the truth, which the arrangement cannot be sound without.

By this, He, the Exalted, only intends to draw attention to the soundness of the Resurrection and of recompense. He, the Exalted, says: We did not create creation in vain, by bringing them into being and giving them life as We wish, then causing them to perish without a test through obedience, command and prohibition, and without rewarding the obedient for his obedience and the disobedient for his disobedience. Rather, We created that so that We may try whom We wish of Our creatures with whatever trial We wish of commands and prohibitions, ﴿that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best [reward]﴾.

﴿But most of them do not know﴾: He, the Exalted, says: But most of these polytheists in God do not know that God created that for them. Therefore they do not fear, for what they commit of the wrath of God, a punishment, nor do they hope, for any good they may do, a reward, because they deny the Return.

* * *

And His saying ﴿The Day when no protector will avail another protector at all﴾

He says: no cousin will repel a cousin, nor a companion his companion, from any of the punishment of Allah that has befallen them. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾: he says, nor will some of them help others, so that they seek refuge from the one who has inflicted punishment upon them, as they used to do in the world.

As narrated:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿The Day when no protector will avail another protector at all﴾ ... the verse: The means will be severed on that day, O son of Adam, and people will turn to their deeds. Whoever gains good on that day will be made happy by it, in what remains of his own sake; and whoever gains evil on that day will be made miserable by it, in what remains of his own sake.

* * *

And His saying ﴿Except for whom Allah has shown mercy﴾

The grammarians differed regarding the position (i'rab) of "man" (whoever) in His saying ﴿Except for whom Allah has shown mercy﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "illa man rahima Allah" (except whom Allah has shown mercy) is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "yunsarun" (they will be helped); and if you wish, you may make it a subject (mubtada') and supply its predicate, meaning: except whoever Allah has shown mercy to, so he will avail him. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said regarding His saying ﴿Except for whom Allah has shown mercy﴾: the believers intercede for one another. So if you wish, make "man" in the nominative position, as if you said: no one will stand except so-and-so; and if you wish, make it accusative as an exception (istithna') disjoined from the beginning of the sentence, meaning: "O Allah, except whom Allah has shown mercy."

Others among them said: its meaning is that no protector will avail another protector anything, except whom Allah has permitted to intercede. He said: it cannot be a substitute for what is in "yunsarun," because the exception is affirmed while the first clause is negated, and a substitute can only carry the meaning of the first. He said: likewise it cannot be a new independent sentence, because an exception is not begun as a new sentence.

The most correct of these opinions, in the view of the truth, is that it stands in the nominative position, meaning: on the Day when no protector will avail another protector anything, except whoever among them Allah has shown mercy to, for he will avail him by interceding for him with his Lord.

* * *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, describes Himself: Indeed Allah is the Mighty in His retribution against His enemies, the Merciful toward His friends and the people of His obedience.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed the tree of zaqqum, whose fruit He made the food of the disbeliever in Hell, is like molten lead or silver, or whatever is melted in the fire when it is melted by it, its heat having become intense and its heat having become fierce in extreme blackness.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiya narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Maymun narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah regarding His words: ﴿like murky oil that scorches the faces﴾, he said: "ʿAbd Allah entered the treasury, took out remnants that were in it, and kindled the fire upon them until they gleamed. * * *

And His words: ﴿in the bellies﴾

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Madina, Basra and Kufa read "taghli" with the letter ta', meaning that the tree of zaqqum boils in their bellies, so they made "taghli" feminine to agree with the feminine "tree." Some reciters of Kufa read ﴿yaghli﴾, meaning: the food of the sinner boils, or the murky oil boils. Some of them made it masculine to agree with the masculine "food," the sense being that the food is what boils in their bellies; and some made it masculine to agree with "murky oil," taking it as an adjective of the murky oil that boils.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known readings, sound in meaning, so whichever of them the reader recites is correct. ﴿like the boiling of scalding water﴾ means: that boils in the bellies of these wretched ones like the boiling of scalding water, which is heated, over which fire has been kindled until the intensity of its heat has reached its utmost. It is said: "hamim" and "mahmum," because it is turned from the passive sense to the form fa'il, as one says "qatil" from "maqtul."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 44, verses 43–46:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum (43) is the food of the sinful (44), like murky oil; it boils in the bellies (45) like the boiling of scalding water (46).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum﴾, which He informed us grows at the root of the Hellfire, which He made food for the people of the Hellfire, whose fruit in Hell is the food of the sinner in this world with respect to his Lord. Al-athim (the sinful) is the one possessing sin (ithm), and ithm comes from athima, yaʾthamu, so he is athim. What is meant here is the one whose sin is disbelief in his Lord, rather than other sins.

* And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, that Abu al-Darda' was teaching a man: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinful﴾, and the man said: "The food of the orphan." Abu al-Darda' said: "Say: indeed the tree of zaqqum is the food of the wicked (fajir)."

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿIsa narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: "If a single drop of the zaqqum of Hell were sent down to the world, it would corrupt the livelihoods of people."

* Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Muʿawiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from Hammam, who said: Abu al-Darda' was teaching a man: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinful﴾. He said: the man began to say: "Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the orphan." When Abu al-Darda' repeated it to him many times and saw that he did not understand, he said: "Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the wicked (fajir)."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinful﴾: "Abu Jahl."
